newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mediators to work against church arson.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mediators to work against church arson.

text.p: Federal mediators and a leading black church group agreed Wednesday to take new steps to prevent church burnings and bombings and help communities and congregations rebuild after arson attacks.

The Justice Department's Community Relations Service and the Congress of National Black Churches said they would exchange information on preventing church arson and coordinate federal and private assistance when churches are burned.

"It's a climate of bigotry, hatred and intolerance that fuels hate crimes and arsons against places of worship," Assistant Attorney General and CRS Director Rose Ochi told a news conference. She said the Justice Department would also work with the black church group to encourage multiracial efforts in rebuilding churches.
"You have to deal with community education," southeast CRS director Ozell Sutton said. "You have to make law enforcement more conscious and vigilant."
A national church arson task force this month said it could find no evidence of a national conspiracy in 429 church burnings that have occurred since the beginning of 1995.
"The lack of a conspiracy makes the problem more difficult to work with," Sutton said. "If there was a conspiracy we could zero in on a certain group."

The CRS said more than 180 churches in 13 Southern states have been burned and desecrated in the past year and a half. The agency said it has provided reconciliation services to more than 150 local communities after church arsons.
